'''Emanuele Quercigh''' (born 1934 in [[Naples]], [[Italy]]) is an Italian particle physicist who works since 1964 at [[CERN]], most known for the discovery of [[Quark–gluon plasma|quark-gluon plasma (QGP)]]. Quercigh moved as a child to [[Friuli-Venezia Giulia|Friuli]] with his mother and his younger brother after the early death of his father.<ref name=":1">{{Cite web|title="Consensus" and "Balance": Interview with Emanuele Quercigh|url=http://alicematters.web.cern.ch/?q=content/node/1106|date=11 June 2018|website=ALICE Matters|url-status=live|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20191102190520/http://alicematters.web.cern.ch/?q=content/node/1106|archive-date=2 November 2019|access-date=2020-05-07}}</ref> Quercigh studied physics at the [[University of Milan]] in Italy, where he became assistant of professor [[Giuseppe Occhialini]] in 1959.

In 1964 Quercigh moved to [[Geneva]], [[Switzerland]], where he took up a position as fellow at [[CERN]] and subsequently became a staff physicist.<ref>{{Cite book|last1=Redondi|first1=Pietro|url=https://books.google.com/books?id=x3HZmlP9MpoC&pg=PA121|title=The Scientific Legacy of Beppo Occhialini|last2=Sironi|first2=Giorgio|last3=Tucci|first3=Pascuale|last4=Vegni|first4=Guido|date=2007-05-11|publisher=Springer Science & Business Media|isbn=978-3-540-37354-4|pages=112|language=en}}</ref> Initially Quercigh took part in various experiments using the [[2 m Bubble Chamber (CERN)|CERN 2 m Bubble Chamber]]. Then he proposed and led, together with David Lord, the ERASME project, a machine for scanning and measuring film from [[Big European Bubble Chamber|BEBC]].

In 1974, Quercigh was appointed spokesperson of the [[T209 experiment]], a bubble chamber experiment studying high statistics 8.25 GeV/c K–p, which discovered the φ(1850) particle–the first Regge recurrence of the [[Phi meson|φ meson]]–and performed a detailed study of the lifetime of the [[Sigma baryon|Ω–baryon]], as well as a first evaluation of its spin.<ref>{{Cite journal|last1=Al-Harran|first1=S.|last2=Amirzadeh|first2=J.|last3=Baubillier|first3=M.|last4=Bloodworth|first4=I.J.|last5=Bossen|first5=G.J.|last6=Burns|first6=A.|last7=Carney|first7=J.N.|last8=Cox|first8=G.F.|last9=Dore|first9=U.|last10=Gavillet|first10=Ph.|last11=Kinson|first11=J.B.|year=1981|title=Observation of a K enhancement at 1.85 GeV in the reaction|journal=Physics Letters B|language=en|volume=101|issue=5|pages=357–360|doi=10.1016/0370-2693(81)90063-0}}</ref><ref>{{Cite journal|last1=Baubillier|first1=M.|last2=Bloodworth|first2=I.J.|last3=Bossen|first3=G.J.|last4=Burns|first4=A.|last5=Carney|first5=J.N.|last6=Corden|first6=M.J.|last7=Cowan|first7=C.A.|last8=Cox|first8=G.F.|last9=De Lima|first9=C.J.|last10=Dixon|first10=D.|last11=Gavillet|first11=Ph.|year=1978|title=A study of the lifetime and spin of Ω<sup>−</sup> produced in K<sup>−</sup>p interactions at 8.25 GeV/c|journal=Physics Letters B|language=en|volume=78|issue=2–3|pages=342–346|doi=10.1016/0370-2693(78)90036-9}}</ref>

As of 1979 Quercigh was the leading scientist for various [[Super Proton Synchrotron|CERN SPS]] experiments using the Omega Spectrometer, a facility he promoted with colleagues already in 1968,<ref>{{Cite book|last1=Baker|first1=W. F.|url=https://cds.cern.ch/record/299898/|title=The OMEGA project: Proposal for a large magnet and spark chamber studying [[quantum chromodynamics]] (QCD) processes, [[hadron spectroscopy]] and particle and soft photon production mechanisms.<ref>{{cite encyclopedia|last1=Beusch|publisher=World Scientific|bibcode=2017cern.book...39C|editor-first2=Simone|editor-last2=Gilardoni|title=OMEGA: towards the electronic bubble chamber|isbn=978-981-4749-13-8|doi=10.1142/9789814749145_0003|language=en|date=2017|first1=Werner|pages=74–77|volume=27|chapter=Advanced Series on Directions in High Energy Physics (Chapter 3: The Proton Synchrotron (PS): At the Core of the CERN Accelerators)|editor-first=Donald|editor-last=Cundy|first2=Emanuele|last2=Quercigh|url=https://cds.cern.ch/record/2312566}}</ref> This activity focused on the production of [[baryon]]s and [[Antibaryon|anti-baryons]] carrying one or more [[strange quark]]s in [[Heavy-Ion collisions|heavy-ion collisions]].<ref>{{Citation|last1=Koch|first1=Peter|chapter=From Strangeness Enhancement to Quark–Gluon Plasma Discovery|title=Walter Greiner Memorial Volume|pages=221–248|year=2018|publisher=World Scientific|language=en|doi=10.1142/9789813234284_0016|isbn=978-981-323-427-7|last2=Müller|first2=Berndt|last3=Rafelski|first3=Johann|author-link2=Berndt Müller|author-link3=Johann Rafelski|arxiv=1708.08115}}</ref> Quercigh was the CERN contact man or spokesman for the [[WA85 experiment|WA85]],<ref>{{Cite book|url=https://cds.cern.ch/record/612556|title=Proposal: study of high energy nucleus-nucleus interactions using the <math>\Omega</math>' spectrometer equipped with a multiparticle high p<sub>T</sub> detector|date=1984|editor-last=CERN. G.|last3=Di Bari|first3=D.|date=1991|others=CERN. Geneva. SPS-LEAR Experiments Committee}}</ref><ref>{{Cite journal|last1=Antinori|first1=F.|last2=Bakke|first2=H.|last3=Beusch|first3=W.|last4=Bloodworth|first4=I.J.|last5=Caliandro|first5=R.|last6=Carrer|first6=N.|last7=Di Bari|first7=D.|last8=Di Liberto|first8=S.|last9=Elia|first9=D.|last10=Evans|first10=D.|last11=Fanebust|first11=K.|year=1999|title=Production of strange and multistrange hadrons in nucleus—nucleus collisions at the SPS|journal=Nuclear Physics A|language=en|volume=661|issue=1–4|pages=130–139|doi=10.1016/S0375-9474(99)85015-5|bibcode=1999NuPhA.661..130A|url=https://cds.cern.ch/record/477522}}</ref> experiments addressing [[strangeness and quark-gluon plasma]].<ref>{{Cite journal|last1=Quercigh|first1=Emanuele|last2=Rafelski|first2=Johann|author-link2=Johann Rafelski|year=2000|title=A strange quark plasma|url=https://cds.cern.ch/record/715770|journal=Physics World|volume=13|issue=10|pages=37–42|doi=10.1088/2058-7058/13/10/35|issn=0953-8585}}</ref> When CERN announced the observation of [[Quark–gluon plasma|the QGP]] in February 2000,<ref>{{Cite web|title=New State of Matter created at CERN|url=https://home.cern/news/press-release/cern/new-state-matter-created-cern|website=CERN|language=en|access-date=2020-05-07}}</ref> he presented the [[strange particle]] production results on behalf of these collaborations.

Together with [[Jürgen Schukraft]] and [[Hans Gutbrod]], Quercigh laid down the foundations of the [[Large Hadron Collider|LHC]] [[ALICE experiment]]. He was then elected as the first chairman of the ALICE Collaboration Board on 20 April 1994 for the period from 1994 to 1998.<ref>{{Cite web|title=Happy 25th birthday, ALICE!|url=https://home.cern/news/news/experiments/happy-25th-birthday-alice|last=Greco|first=Virginia|date=13 April 2018|website=CERN|language=en|url-status=live|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20191102064013/https://home.cern/news/news/experiments/happy-25th-birthday-alice|archive-date=2 November 2019|access-date=2020-05-08}}</ref><ref>{{Cite web|title=Quercigh Emanuele|url=https://www.ropipublications.com/quercigh-emanuele/|date=2015-07-06|website=Ropi Publications|language=en|url-status=live|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20200508035245/https://www.ropipublications.com/quercigh-emanuele/|archive-date=8 May 2020|access-date=2020-05-07}}</ref>

After retirement from CERN in 1999, Quercigh is honorary staff member. In the years  2000, 2001 and 2003 he was guest professor at the [[University of Padua]].
